chapter_theme: Last songs at Vayalur (வயலூர், 2 of 2): the courtesans' showing and the dangerous beauty of women, answered by a litany of the Goddess's names and by the longest plea of the group, which sets the 'small pleasure' of union against the three impurities removed and the sea of Siva's release.
structure_note: 915 repeats the காட்டி refrain of 901; 916 turns from women to a long list of the Goddess's names; 917 is a very long song in which the confession, the doctrinal plea and the battle in drum syllables each run to many lines.

915.reading: With the refrain காட்டி ('showing'), the poet lists what courtesans show, the loosened girdle, spread hair, rolling spear eyes, shining body, staged drama, invitations to their houses, Kama's rules recited, breasts, laughter with anyone and pretended feeling, and asks whether he will perish by the desire they show. The praise uses the same verb for Murugan: he showed love, drew out and showed jnana as the guru who taught the old Tamil sage, gave the three worlds, raised the cock banner, made the peacock dance, heated the great mountain, and guarded the gods' heads, at Vayalur.
915.nuance: The one verb carries both halves: the women 'show' to deceive (விரகாலே, வேசைகள் மயக்கைக் காட்ட), and the Lord 'shows' jnana (ஞானமும் எடுத்துக் காட்டி). மூதமிழ் முனிக்குக் கூட்டு குருநாதா is Murugan as Agastya's teacher of Tamil.

916.reading: The poet says women's eyes are crueller than a sword's edge, poison, Yama's tread and arrows, and lists their nectar mouths, white smiles, sweet 'come, sit', rosewater, saffron, sandal and musk, breasts, hips and navel, the hut where maya dwells, and asks whether he will cease to be bewildered on seeing such harlots. The praise is a litany of the Goddess, Kali, Tripurai, Sundari, Nili, Gauri, Sankari, Sivai, Kundali, Chandika, Ambika, Tryambaki whom Lakshmi, Saraswati, Rati, Arundhati and Indra's queen worship, Vishnu's sister, and names Murugan her son, who removes the sorrow of those who think of the vel and peacock, at Mélai Vayalur.
916.nuance: மாயை குடிகொள் குடம்பை, the nest where maya lives, calls the woman's body the dwelling of illusion. The praise gives most of its length to the Goddess's names, so the song is as much hers as her son's, as in 32.

917.reading: Over many lines the poet describes perfumed women who roam the streets and take young men's wealth with their lives, and a long scene of lovemaking, lips tasted like nectar and honey, marks of nail and teeth, the bird-cries learned from Kama's art, and the lovers' points of the moon from foot to crown, an experience 'one cannot leave even for a moment'; knowing this union a small pleasure, he asks when, the three impurities cut and the mind made one, he will reach the boundless space and light, the manifest Siva-tattva and the sea of release. The praise, after drum syllables, shakes peaks, seas, the eight elephants and the serpent Sesha, fills the field with blood, vultures and jackals, and names the Saravanabhava of Vayali who taught Agastya the Tamil of verse, music and drama.
917.nuance: புணரும் இது சிறு சுகம்: the poet judges union a small pleasure, after describing it at length as one that 'cannot be left for a moment' (ஒரு பொழுதும் விடலரிது). The lunar kalas waxing and waning on the body (குமுத பதி கலை குறைகலை நிறைகலை) come from the love manuals. The plea runs through Siddhanta terms: திரிமலம் அற்று, கருத்து ஒருமை உற்று, சிவ தத்வ ப்ரசித்தி, முத்திச் சிவக் கடல். The division of several lines in the plea is unsure.

links.note: Two Vayalur songs on the one refrain காட்டி, 'showing': in both the courtesans show their bodies and arts to deceive, and 915 turns the same verb on Murugan, who shows jnana.
